shortName: Rush Medical College of Rush University Medical Center
additionalCoursework: Rush Medical College also recommends coursework in Anatomy, Physiology, and subjects that provide exposure to the social determinants of health and disparities in healthcare outcomes. Examples include, but are not limited to, Sociology, Public Health, Political Science, Global Health, Bioethics, Urban Studies, History, and Economics.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
RMC seeks to attract a student body that is representative of the national population, which includes recruiting applicants from groups underrepresented in medicine. Once on campus, we foster curricular and extracurricular environments where students combine their backgrounds and perspectives to collectively solve problems, address the social determinants of health, and enhance their abilities to work with diverse peers and patients.

Health equity content is incorporated throughout the RMC curriculum. Additionally, the four-year Health Equity and Social Justice Leadership Program within RMC empowers students to advocate for health equity throughout their careers.

Additionally, the Office of Student Diversity & Community Engagement collaboratively hosts monthly events to honor various groups’ backgrounds and heritages. The office also supports and mentors all affinity groups that raise awareness of and appreciation for the many types of diversity at Rush.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Senior Associate Dean for Education will decide each request for leave of absence and will determine the duration of the leave and the conditions, if any, for resuming active student status. A student may be on a leave of absence without first stating in writing to the Senior Associate Dean his/her intent to return to the College to complete the requirements for the MD degree. The Senior Associate Dean may consult with the Committee on Student Evaluation and Promotion before approving a leave of absence for a student with academic deficiencies.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Community service is an integral part of Rush's culture; it is who Rush is and what Rush does. Using their distinct skills and talents, students are eager to make an impact within the communities we serve. Through the Rush Community Service Initiatives Program (RCSIP), students, staff, faculty, and clinicians have a variety of opportunities to give back and make a difference locally and beyond. In fact, the efforts of RCSIP were recognized by the AAMC, which awarded RMC the 2020 Spencer Foreman Award for Outstanding Community Engagement. In addition to over 30 RCSIP programs, the Offices of Student Life and Student Diversity & Community Engagement sponsor over 40 active student organizations and affinity groups that enhance the co-curricular lives of Rush students. Student Life often hosts campus-wide programming and encourages the exploration of Chicago’s cultural, educational, and social resources by regularly offering discounted museum, theater, sports, and movie tickets.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Rush University is a private, non-profit health sciences institution based just west of Chicago’s Loop on the campus of Rush University Medical Center (RUMC). Located within the Illinois Medical District (IMD), RUMC is the primary clinical site for RMC and is a nationally-ranked academic medical center specializing in leading-edge patient care and research. Our other major teaching affiliate, the John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County, is a block away and serves as the largest safety-net hospital in Chicago. The entire Rush system, through its anchor mission strategy, is dedicated to improving the health of the communities we serve, including in the Near West Side, where RMC is located. For more information about RUMC, Stroger, and IMD, visit https://rsh.md/RUMC, https://rsh.md/STROGER, and https://rsh.md/IMD, respectively.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: RMC supports incoming students’ housing search throughout the spring and summer prior to matriculation. RMC hosts presentations with Chicago apartment review companies, whose services are free of charge. During Admitted Student Visit Day, current students discuss their favorite of Chicago’s 77 unique communities, as well as detail their housing and transportation experiences during the pre-clerkship and clerkship years. Finally, RMC student ambassadors facilitate housing-related conversations among incoming students on the accepted-student Facebook page; many accepted applicants find their first roommates on the site.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Rush University’s LGBTQ+ student affinity group, Rush Pride, offers a robust program of social, service, and advocacy activities. Faculty who identify as LGBTQ+ are well-represented throughout the institution and are involved in many aspects of undergraduate medical education. Rush University Medical Center has been a Healthcare Equality Index (HEI) Leader since 2009, and the Rush System for Health launched Affirm: The Rush Center for Gender, Sexuality & Reproductive Health in 2020. A fourth-year LGBTQ+ health elective is also offered.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities:
In keeping with its goal to promote diversity among its student population, Rush University is committed to attracting and educating students who will help to make the population of health care professionals reflective of the national population, including individuals with disabilities. In addition, Rush University is committed to ensuring equal access to its facilities, programs and services are available to students with disabilities.

Students with physical, chronic health conditions, temporary conditions/injuries, sensory, learning, and/or psychological disabilities are encouraged to engage with the Office of Student Accessibility Services to confidentially document their diagnoses and request reasonable accommodations to remove access-related barriers they may experience on campus, in academics, and in clinical settings. 

More information about the Office of Student Accessibility Services can be found here: https://bit.ly/RU-OSAS.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Rush University's Center for Clinical Wellness (CCW) seeks to address three primary goals: the creation of a culture of wellness, including programs to address burnout, support resilience, and increase joy in work; increased support for mental health, including access to care, reduction in stigma, and strategic partnerships to prevent suicide; and production of leading research through an emphasis on data and analytics.

Members of the wellness team are licensed behavioral health professionals with a range of backgrounds, all with a master's degree or above. All services, including coaching and counseling, are free of charge. For more information, visit https://bit.ly/RushCCW.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
At RMC, campus culture is defined by collaboration, inclusivity, and mutual respect, creating a sense of belonging for all community members. Students thrive in a supportive environment where they are encouraged to ask questions and seek mentorship, prioritizing teamwork over competition. Through mentorship programs and engagement opportunities, Rush ensures students are well-supported as they prepare for meaningful careers.

Beyond academics, RMC students impact the community, serving over 10,000 individuals annually through initiatives that improve healthcare access, promote health education, and build pathways for future healthcare professionals. The dynamic, multicultural setting of Chicago further enriches the campus experience, offering students opportunities to engage with the city’s diverse arts, culture, and innovation.

RMC also has a thriving research community, where students, faculty, and staff collaborate on cutting-edge research across various healthcare fields.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Third- and fourth-year students are ultimately responsible for arranging their own transportation to clerkship sites. Although many clinical experiences for Rush Medical College students take place on or very near campus, students should plan to travel during the clerkship years. Some sites are accessible by public transportation while other sites require access to a car. Resources are available to help support transportation needs.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: The Medical Student Affairs (MSA) team offers holistic programming to foster students’ success in their academic, career and professional endeavors. For more information, visit https://bit.ly/RMCMSA.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Support is offered to students at all academic success levels. Support facilitators include learning specialists, peer and resident educators, and academic advisors. Faculty have an open-door policy.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Patient exposure begins immediately in the M1 year and continues during curricular and co-curricular activities throughout all four years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: M1 and M2 students access course content online prior to class and then apply the information in person during faculty-facilitated, case-based, small-group activities (i.e., flipped classroom model).
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Students complete eight core clerkships, one sub-internship, and a minimum of 24 weeks of electives from among dozens of offerings.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Rush Medical College will provide residency programs with descriptive individualized student data in an unranked fashion.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: All classes are small-group sessions with required attendance. Online lectures are not provided in lieu of attendance but are assigned to prepare students for and supplement their in-person sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
RMC provides a comprehensive background in medical science and clinical practice through a four-year curriculum in an environment that fosters a commitment to exceptional and compassionate patient care, as well as attitudes of inquiry and life-long learning.

Organ system-based pre-clerkship courses integrate normal and disease states including often-overlooked content (e.g., obstetrics & gynecology, pediatrics, and geriatrics). An emphasis is placed on the clinical application of basic science knowledge, communication and physical exam skills, social determinants of health, humanism in medicine, personal wellness, medical ethics, health care economics, biostatistics, and many other topics taught in the context of patient cases. Core clerkships are offered in medicine, surgery, ob-gyn, neurology, psychiatry, pediatrics, primary care, and emergency medicine. Longitudinal leadership programs in Family Medicine and Health Equity & Social Justice Leadership are options for incoming students. More information on these programs can be found at https://bit.ly/RMCLongitudinalPrograms under the "Longitudinal Specialty Programs" section.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The Family Medicine Leadership Program is a four-year longitudinal curriculum for up to five medical students per year. The curriculum emphasizes patient-centered, community-based, interdisciplinary learning as well as the development of leadership and advocacy skills. 

EXPLORE Rush pairs M1 and M2 students with authentic clinical, research, and/or advocacy work to reinforce and invigorate their classroom learning during the pre-clerkship years. Students are encouraged to be the architects of their own education, selecting experiences based on their interests and learning goals. Students may select a new experience each term (for a total of five different experiences over the first two years) or continue with a single experience for two semesters or more if they prefer. Students interested in the primary care disciplines may focus their EXPLORE experiences on primary care or dedicate some of their time to the many specialties that support this discipline.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: M1 students can choose to expand their research knowledge by taking the Basic Biomedical Research elective, which includes lectures, a journal club, and written assignments to further introduce students to the theory and practice of clinical, behavioral, and basic science research. Additionally, M1 students can apply for the Summer Research Fellowship, which is a six-week program for students working with faculty on basic science, clinical, or community-based research. All students have the opportunity to independently conduct bench, clinical, and community-based research with faculty. Information about Rush University-specific research can be found at https://rsh.md/RESEARCH. Additionally, information about research opportunities for students can be found at https://bit.ly/RMCResearchOpportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: The first two years of the RMC curriculum use a flipped-classroom approach.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: While not required, Rush offers many service opportunities for students, including the Rush Community Service Initiatives Program (RCSIP). For more information, visit https://bit.ly/RushRCSIP.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Research opportunities for students can be found at https://bit.ly/RMCResearchOpportunities.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Generally, students complete their core clerkships and sub-internship at Rush University Medical Center and/or the John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Courses in the pre-clerkship years (M1 and M2) are graded as Pass/Fail. Courses in the clerkship years (M3 and M4) are graded as Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail.
medSchoolCurriculum.languageInstructions: English is the language of instruction. Beginner and Intermediate Medical Spanish electives are offered to students in their M1 year.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: RMC, located in Chicago, offers medical students a supportive environment where they can gain in-depth clinical experience from our renowned practitioner-teachers. Founded in 1837, RMC has an acclaimed history as one of the first medical colleges in the Midwest and continues to make major contributions to medical science and education through research and clinical trials. Our students serve a diverse population of patients from across Chicago and beyond due to our unique location within the Illinois Medical District, which includes our clinical affiliates: Rush University Medical Center (RUMC), an internationally-recognized academic health center, and the John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital of Cook County, one of the nation’s largest safety-net hospitals. Driven by Rush's anchor mission, our students pride themselves in making a difference by volunteering in numerous service opportunities aimed at helping the under- and un-insured within our own community.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Rush Medical College (RMC) is one of three colleges within Rush University (RU), the academic arm of the Rush University System for Health (RUSH). The missions of RMC and RU have been adopted in support of Rush's mission, which is to improve the health of the individuals and diverse communities we serve through the integration of outstanding patient care, education, research, and community partnerships.

Rush University champions a learning environment in health and biomedical sciences through collaboration, education, research, and equity for our students, faculty, staff, and the communities we serve.

RMC's mission is to nurture, through a supportive and dynamic learning community, the development of empathic, proficient physicians dedicated to continuous learning, innovation, and excellence in clinical practice, education, research, and service.

RMC seeks to interview and matriculate applicants who have demonstrated their alignment with the various Rush mission statements through their direct patient care experiences, longitudinal commitments to service, leadership and extracurricular activities, and research endeavors.
medSchoolInformation.videoDescription: At Rush, you’ll enjoy small class sizes and hands-on learning in a state-of-the-art medical center led by faculty who are accomplished practitioners and researchers. You’ll feel supported in a learning community that connects disciplines and promotes diversity.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes; RMC complies with the Illinois Medical School Matriculant Criminal History Records Check Act by participating in the AMCAS-facilitated criminal background check service for accepted applicants.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: RMC's Plan to Enroll and Deposit deadlines are April 30, 2027. Applicants who have decided not to attend RMC should withdraw their applications ahead of this deadline in fairness to other applicants.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: For applicants who submit individual letters, RMC suggests the submission of one academic letter (which does not need to originate from a science faculty member), one professional non-academic letter, and one personal letter. Further guidance regarding letters of recommendation can be found on our website at https://rsh.md/LOR under the "Letters of Recommendation" section.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: RMC prefers pre-medical committee letters for those applicants whose institutions provide this service; committee letters are acceptable with or without the inclusion of ancillary individual letters. Letter packets and up to three individual letters are acceptable alternatives for those without pre-professional committees or who are unable or ineligible to participate in the committee review process. Guidelines regarding letters of recommendation can be found on our website at https://rsh.md/LOR under the "Letters of Recommendation" section.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants invited to interview will receive additional logistical information via email.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: RMC will host virtual interviews for the 2026-2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: RMC will host virtual interviews for the 2026-2027 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Secondary application invitations are extended to qualified applicants after an initial review of the primary AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: The completed application is due August 3. Additional information regarding the EDP can be found on RMC’s website at https://rsh.md/EDP.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: In-state and out-of-state applications are considered equally, and tuition rates are the same for both in-state and out-of-state students.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Applications are accepted from both in-state and out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Each applicant must be a U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, or of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), refugee, or asylee status.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: RMC welcomes applicants who are U.S. permanent residents or are of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), asylee or refugee status.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: RMC welcomes applicants of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) status.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Applicants to RMC must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for admission to the MD program: 1) be U.S. citizens, U.S. permanent residents, Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) status, asylee status, or refugee status; 2) have completed a bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university accredited in the United States or Canada; 3) have taken and had scores reported for the Medical College Admissions Test (MCAT); and 4) have taken the Casper situational judgment test (SJT).
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The RMC admissions committee considers MCAT scores as part of its holistic review of applicants. Our reviewers and interviewers are blinded to GPA and MCAT scores in support of the holistic review of applicants.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: As part of RMC's holistic review process, applicants should demonstrate a strong academic foundation, including the MCAT, to be successful in RMC's unique flipped classroom curriculum. Please visit the RMC website (https://rsh.md/ADMREQ, under the "MCAT & GPA" section) for comprehensive details on the attributes of successful applicants.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: As part of RMC's holistic review process, applicants should demonstrate a strong academic foundation, including GPA, to be successful in RMC's unique flipped classroom curriculum. Please visit the RMC website (https://rsh.md/ADMREQ, under the "MCAT & GPA" section) for comprehensive details on the attributes of successful applicants.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Applicants who do not meet the minimum undergraduate metrics will continue to be considered for admission if they possess postbacc or graduate GPAs of 3.5 or greater and have completed, at the time of application, at least 24 postbacc or graduate credit hours in BCPM basic science preparatory coursework. Note: Prospective applicants should review MSAR and RMC’s website (https://rsh.md/ADMREQ) for comprehensive details on the attributes of successful applicants.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: RMC recommends that applicants seeking additional academic enhancement consider preparatory postbacc and graduate programs that will build their foundation in the BCPM basic sciences.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: While RMC accepts community college coursework, it is highly recommended that higher-level basic science coursework and/or prerequisite coursework be taken at a four-year institution.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: RMC accepts letters of intent, letters of interest, and notices of significant updates or achievements throughout the application cycle.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: RMC's technical standards can be found here under the "Technical standards for admission & promotion" section: https://rsh.md/ADMREQ.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Accepted applicants begin receiving financial aid packages in early spring. Packages meet 100 percent of demonstrated financial need and include grants, scholarships, and loans.

medSchoolPrograms.info: The David Jones Peck, MD Pre-Medical Education Program (DJP PEP) is an in-person summer program intended to prepare aspiring, motivated pre-medical students with the means to strengthen their ability and readiness to become competitive and successful applicants to medical school. It is named after David Jones Peck, MD, an 1847 RMC alumnus who was the first African American to earn a medical degree from a US medical school. This program includes academic enrichment in the basic sciences; AMCAS application and interview preparation; community service experiences; medical school financial planning; peer and faculty mentorship; and more. Program participants will also have the opportunity to learn about health disparities and illnesses prevalent in underserved communities. For additional information, please email RMC_Admissions@rush.edu.

Although RMC does not offer formalized combined degree programs, some students have pursued other degree and research programs on their own after matriculation. Students interested in these opportunities discuss with their advisors if such options are compatible with their plans of study and future goals. The senior associate dean provides final approval of such pursuits.

Secondary Rush Medical College (RMC) Application Deadline (Regular MD)

Through AMCAS, accepted applicants may select “Plan to Enroll” beginning February 19th. This communicates to all schools that an applicant has decided where they plan to enroll. Only one school can be selected; however this information can be updated as applicants continue to finalize their decisions. Applicants may continue to hold multiple acceptance offers and waitlist offers at this time.

Accepted applicants who are holding acceptances at multiple schools must narrow their selection to no more than three schools. The AAMC asks that applicants decline offers, via email, from all other schools on or before April 15th. Applicants may continue to hold waitlist offers after April 15th.
Rush Medical College (RMC) Plan to Enroll and Deposit Deadline

Through AMCAS, accepted applicants may select “Commit to Enroll” beginning April 30th. This selection indicates a final decision has been made regarding the school in which an applicant plans to matriculate. The AAMC asks that applicants notify all other schools of this decision by declining their offers of admission and/or waitlist offers.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: The typical number of waitlist positions varies from year to year.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: RMC's waitlist is not ranked; applications are reviewed to determine future acceptances. Waitlisted applicants are encouraged to upload updates to the applicant portal throughout the cycle.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
RMC requires the following prerequisite coursework at time of application:

- One academic YEAR of Chemistry, with one COURSE being Biochemistry. One COURSE of Organic Chemistry is recommended.
- One academic YEAR of Biology, with one COURSE being Cell Biology or a related course focused on cell biology.
- One academic YEAR of lab work in Biology and/or Chemistry
- One COURSE of Physics (can be fulfilled with AP credit)
- One COURSE of Algebra or higher-level math (can be fulfilled with AP credit)
- One academic YEAR of English Composition

Applicants who received AP credit in Biology or Chemistry are required to take advanced science coursework in the corresponding area of study. Students are recommended to take Biology coursework within 5 years of application. Students are also encouraged to complete coursework (e.g. sociology, public health, political science, global health) that provide exposure to content about social determinants of health and disparities in healthcare outcomes.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: RMC holistically reviews applicants' experiences, attributes, and academic qualifications in order to select individuals who align with our mission and who will develop into life-long learners and vital members of the medical community as students, practitioners, educators, and researchers serving the needs of a diverse and changing population. Desired attributes include community service orientation; academic excellence; professionalism, integrity, and ethics; social, interpersonal, and oral communication and teamwork; clinical experience; research; leadership; resilience and adaptability; and reliability and dependability.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: RMC seeks applicants who demonstrate longitudinal commitments to providing care through their quality, direct-patient care experiences (shadowing is not considered a direct-patient care experience). All applicants are expected to have direct patient care experience prior to submitting their primary applications. We recognize many applicants have had their clinical plans altered by the pandemic and all applicants invited to complete RMC’s secondary application will have the opportunity to explain how the pandemic affected their paths to medical school.
